sasha (customer): Hey team — since this morning our Dedicated pool for acct `acme-ux` started returning a lot of 429s even though we reserved capacity. Latency spikes too. Any idea?

maria (support): Sorry you're hitting this, sasha. Can you paste a few example request IDs + timestamps? Also, are you using the reserved pool token or the org key?

sasha (customer): sample: req=rid_01F4T9Z2, ts=2024-10-11T09:12:03Z, header X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0, got 429. We're hitting via dedicated API key (reserved pool). Not using org key.

maria (support): thx. I see an outgoing auto-alert from deploy-bot about a capacity config change at 08:45 — cc @chris (infra) & @kevin (eng-sre). Can you confirm if there was a reserved-pool config tweak? :eyes:

chris (infra): I rolled a small change to the burst-window config for reserved pools at 08:44 as part of a rollout. It reduced the short-window burst allowance from 10s to 3s for CPU/GPU slots to smooth billing. Might explain sudden 429s if traffic bursts are >3s.

kevin (eng-sre): Confirming, the token-bucket refill rate stayed the same but bucket depth dropped for all dedicated pools in that rollout. That misaligns with some customers' traffic patterns. Sasha, are your calls bursty (many small parallel requests) or sustained?

sasha (customer): Mostly bursty — we do parallel fan-out per user action (10–20 reqs in ~2s). Before this morning it was fine.

maria (support): OK that matches. Two immediate options: 1) repro locally with `curl` and our key to capture headers; 2) temporarily increase your pool's short-window bucket via a config rollback / per-customer override while we investigate. Which do you prefer?

sasha (customer): override would be great — low risk for us. But if you need a repro I can run a small script.

chris (infra): We can apply a per-pool emergency override to restore prior bucket depth. I'll queue it but want to validate with kevin that it won't degrade cost SLOs for that cluster.

kevin (eng-sre): Go ahead and apply override for `acme-ux-dedicated` to previous values (burst_window=10s, bucket_depth=20). I'll monitor for any side effects. Also adding a temporary rate-limit header passthrough to logs to correlate.

maria (support): Sasha — we'll do the override in ~10m and ping here. In parallel can you run this quick repro and paste output?

maria (support): ```bash
for i in {1..20}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total} %{redirect_url} %{url_effective}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer <DEDICATED_KEY>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate & done; wait
```

sasha (customer): Run it now, output: 10x 200, 10x 429. Example: `200 0.213 - https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate` and `429 0.045 -`. Request IDs: rid_01F4T9Z2, rid_01F4T9Z3, rid_01F4T9Z4.

deploy-bot: [alert] rollout/infra-burst-window v2 deployed by chris at 2024-10-11T08:44:12Z

chris (infra): Thanks, that matches expected behavior when bursts exceed new window. Override applied at 2024-10-11T09:25:30Z for `acme-ux-dedicated`. Please re-run the repro.

sasha (customer): Re-ran the same loop after override: 20x 200. No 429s. Much better, thanks.

maria (support): Great. Next steps: 1) kevin/infra will schedule a canary rollback on that rollout and add a per-customer traffic profile check before applying short-window changes; 2) we'll offer acme a billing-safe grace period if costs bump during the fix; 3) support will follow up with a postmortem and recommended client-side backoff pattern to avoid sync fanouts.

kevin (eng-sre): I'll open infra-ticket INF-4721 to revert the global change and add a gradual rollout gate tied to reserved-pool weight. Also adding metrics: `pool_bucket_depth` and `pool_burst_429_rate` per-customer.

maria (support): Sasha — would you like us to keep the override long-term or do you want us to coordinate a config that preserves your burst profile but maintains global cost constraints?

sasha (customer): Let's coordinate. We'll share traffic logs for the next 48h and accept a short-term override. Thanks for the quick turnaround. :raised_hands:

maria (support): Copy that. Marking this thread resolved for now; we'll post the postmortem link once INF-4721 has updates.

chris (infra): adding note: to reproduce 429 locally: send >bucket_depth concurrent requests within burst_window; check response header `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset` for the token-bucket state. Example 429 payload: `{\n  "error": "rate_limited",\n  "retry_after": 1.2,\n  "request_id": "rid_01F4T9Z2"\n}`

maria (support): thanks everyone. cc @sasha (customer) we'll track billing and SLA impacts separately.

kevin (eng-sre): follow-ups: INF-4721, add canary gating, update docs on reserved-pool burst semantics.

sasha (customer): appreciated.
